first_five_minutes:
Cassy opens /login. The tab says "Welcome home" (app/login/page.tsx:11) and the card greets "WELCOME HOME, CASSANDRA" (app/login/page.tsx:58) before she has typed anything — her name is printed on a public, unauthenticated page. Under the password field: "Private access, by invitation. Your workspace owner can help with access or a password reset." (login-form.tsx:56). Two sentences in, the app has told her (a) she was let in by someone else and (b) there is a man to ask for help. The product does not send invitations at all — access-page.tsx:84 says "No invitation or email was sent."

She signs in. The h1 is "Welcome home, Cassandra." (connected-home.tsx:62) — hard-coded, so it would say the same thing if Michael signed in; the footer of the same page says "Signed in as cassie-fixture@example.test" (connected-home.tsx:191). The left rail says "Kira Stanley / Author workspace" at the top (app-shell.tsx:111) and "Cassandra / Human in command" at the bottom (app-shell.tsx:223-224), with avatars "KS" and "C". Her two names appear as two different people, eight inches apart, on the screen she is being shown as a gift. Above them: "THE COMMAND CENTER" (app-shell.tsx:113).

Her eye goes to the stats band. It reads, in large serif: 08 / 00 / 00 / 00 (connected-home.tsx:144, `padStart(2, "0")`). Three big padded zeros rendered as "OO OO OO". Then "Start with one small thing. Explore at your own pace." (getting-started.tsx:117-118), numbered 01 02 03.

If Michael shows her the demo build instead, the home page ends with a card titled "YOUR BUSINESS TEAM / Eyes on the universe." listing six agents, five of them "Not connected · IDLE" (agent-status.tsx:18-43), and — the moment her desk clears — "The minions are working. Go write. 🖤" (mission-control.tsx:94, desk-page.tsx:110). The browser tab's description, if she ever shares the link, reads "Let Kira write. The agents run the business." (app/layout.tsx:19). Nothing runs. AGENTS.md forbids exactly this.

First click is probably "Take your seat" (mission-control.tsx:100) into Cassandra's Desk. The h1 there: "They bring the evidence. / You bring the instinct." (desk-page.tsx:41-43). "They" has no antecedent, and she has just been assigned intuition while the software gets facts. That framing repeats five times across the app. Net: the workspace is beautiful and she will say so, and underneath it she has been greeted by a name she did not type, credited with instinct rather than expertise, pointed at an owner three times, and told minions are working for her.

scores.verdict: The mechanics of consent are good (upload permission checkbox, spoiler default off, draft-keep choices). The copy around them routes her to a man at every friction point, and her own creation surface has a first-class button for making something for him.

scores.verdict: Genuinely careful mechanics — beforeunload guard, sign-out confirmation, version conflict detection, error copy that always says the text is still there. Undermined by copy that repeatedly warns her drafts are unprotected instead of protecting them, and by an approve button whose irreversibility lives in 10px grey.

scores.verdict: A real design point of view — Cormorant/Manrope pairing, restrained gold-on-charcoal palette, the raven line art, the daily-quote figure with its Gutenberg source. Craft failures are typographic and ethical at once: the app's honest disclosures live in 8px and 10px type while its slogans get 40px serif, and the padded-zero styling produces an "OO OO OO" stat band.

scores.verdict: The provenance discipline is excellent — DEMO badges, MANUAL SNAPSHOT, NEEDS VERIFICATION, model and cost disclosure, "no external action" everywhere. That work is undercut by four concrete false claims shipped in the copy: the site description says agents run the business, two empty states say minions are working, the login page claims access is by invitation when no invitation is ever sent, and the error page asserts browser-local data in connected mode.

top_findings.title: The product claims autonomous agents are working — in metadata, in two empty states, and on a status card
top_findings.problem: app/layout.tsx:19 ships the description "Let Kira write. The agents run the business." mission-control.tsx:94 and desk-page.tsx:110 both say "The minions are working. Go write. 🖤" when her desk clears. agent-status.tsx:18-43 presents six named agents with status pills under the heading "YOUR BUSINESS TEAM / Eyes on the universe." Nothing runs in the background. AGENTS.md working rule 2 forbids exactly this, and the only correction is an 8px line at agent-status.tsx:50.
top_findings.proposed_change: Metadata → "Let Kira write. A private workspace for the business around the books." Both minion strings → "Nothing is waiting on you right now." Agent card → retitle to "WHAT THIS WORKSPACE CAN DO YET", lift the disclaimer above the grid at normal size, map WAITING/IDLE to "Ready when you ask"/"Not built yet". No test pins any of these strings (grep of tests/ for minions, coven, agents returns nothing).

top_findings.title: The app names Michael in four places and points her at "your workspace owner" in eight more
top_findings.problem: plans-page.tsx:104 "Michael can review this plan and activate its tasks." learn-page.tsx:157 gives her creation page a button labelled "Start an idea for Michael". studio-page.tsx:24 makes "an agent idea for Michael" the default starter text in her private thinking space. ads/dashboard.tsx:45 "Michael needs to finish the Facebook Login for Business configuration with ads_read access." Add login-form.tsx:56, settings-page.tsx:119, setup-status.tsx:59 and :72, context-help.tsx:42, connections-page.tsx:108 and :128, learn-page.tsx:18, one-time-sign-in.tsx:73/78/79. The cumulative message on the day she is handed her own workspace is: ask him.
top_findings.proposed_change: Replace every hard-coded first name with the role ("the workspace owner"). Rewrite each owner-gate line to lead with what she can do and mention the gate second — e.g. plans-page.tsx:104 → "This plan is with the workspace owner for review. You can keep editing the details or start another plan." Make the Michael starter one option behind a neutral "Draft an agent idea to share with someone" affordance. Pinned: tests/agent-recipes.test.ts:31-35 and tests/e2e-connected/new-features.spec.ts:31-59 assert the Michael starter — update them in the same change. Whether an Editor should need owner approval to activate plan tasks is the owner's decision; the wording is not.
top_findings.owner_decision_needed: Whether Cassy (Editor) should be able to activate her own marketing-plan tasks without owner review, or whether the gate stays and only the copy changes.

top_findings.title: Kira and Cassandra are treated as two people, and the software wears her pen name over her manuscript
top_findings.problem: connected-library.tsx:67 "Your words become Kira's reference." connected-book-detail.tsx:118 "Let Kira get to know this book." and :130 "What Kira learned". book-detail.tsx:195 "The story belongs to Kira." and :204 "Cassandra's verification". app/[module]/page.tsx:17 lists "Cassandra's audience guidance" as a requirement while :37 says "how readers discover Kira's books". The sidebar carries both identities at once — app-shell.tsx:111 "Kira Stanley / Author workspace" and :223-224 "Cassandra / Human in command", with avatars KS and C. Kira Stanley is Cassy's pen name; the app has made it the name of the AI that reads her book.
top_findings.proposed_change: Never use "Kira" as the actor. Use "this workspace" or "the reader": "Your words stay yours." / "Add a manuscript and this workspace reads it in small steps and shows you the passage behind every finding." / "What this workspace found". Never refer to her in the third person on her own screens — "The story is yours", "your verification", "your audience guidance". top_findings.title: There is no way to delete an uploaded manuscript
top_findings.problem: She uploads an unpublished manuscript behind an explicit permission checkbox (connected-book-detail.tsx:119), and then the product gives her pause, retry, version history and passage search — but no delete. There is no DELETE handler anywhere under app/api/manuscripts/ or app/api/library/, and no component contains a remove/withdraw affordance (verified by grep). The brief asks whether she can "take it back"; today she cannot, and nothing on the page admits it.
top_findings.proposed_change: Tonight, be honest in the manuscript history block (connected-book-detail.tsx:136): "Removing a saved manuscript isn't available in the app yet. Ask the workspace owner to delete a file and its saved passages." The real fix — a DELETE route, cascade to chunks/knowledge, RLS, audit event, confirm dialog — is a product decision plus a migration.
top_findings.owner_decision_needed: Whether to build manuscript deletion (route + cascade + RLS + tests) before the demo, or ship the honest limitation notice now.

top_findings.title: Raw database enums rendered as UI labels
top_findings.problem: approval-card.tsx:78 renders {approval.status} directly, so the pill reads "pending" in lowercase. access-page.tsx:109 renders "Your role: editor". agent-status.tsx:43 renders "WAITING"/"IDLE". raven-page.tsx:122 renders "EXPERIMENTAL". approval-card.tsx:153 labels her own words "Human feedback" — audit vocabulary applied to a woman's sentences.
top_findings.proposed_change: Add a label map for each enum: pending → "Waiting for you", approved → "Approved", rejected → "Rejected"; editor → "Editor — you can create, edit and decide"; WAITING → "Ready when you ask", IDLE → "Not built yet". approval-card.tsx:153 "Human feedback" → "Your note".

what_works: lib/data/inspiration.ts is the best writing in the product and should be the voice model for everything else. The briefDraft bodies are written in her first person ("CURATED REFLECTION · FOR MY REVIEW", "Which published book would I love to put back in a reader's hands?"), the firstStep fields are concrete and small, and the honesty is built into the content rather than bolted on as a disclaimer (inspiration.ts:59 "A few comments are a starting point, not a claim about the whole audience"). Do not touch it.

The manuscript permission checkbox at connected-book-detail.tsx:119 is specific about what is being consented to and what is not: "I have permission to upload this manuscript and have Kira's AI services analyze it privately for book knowledge. This does not approve publishing excerpts." Keep the two-clause shape; only change the word "Kira".

The spoiler gate is real consent, not theatre: book-knowledge.tsx:89 defaults to off, tells her exactly how many findings are hidden, and the manuscript search at :135 requires a separate opt-in checkbox before any excerpt appears. The source dialog at :138 warns that passages "may contain spoilers and [are] not approved marketing copy."

Error copy across the app consistently protects her text: manual-review-form.tsx:99 and :105 "Your text is still here; please try again", learn-page.tsx:93 "It is still here; try again or download a copy", connected-library.tsx:38 "Your entries are still here", book-knowledge.tsx:82 "Your manuscript is unchanged". This is a genuine pattern and it should survive any rewrite.

The approve/reject confirmation at approval-card.tsx:184 states the irreversibility plainly and names what will not happen: "This decision is final: the brief becomes read-only and cannot be reopened or edited. You can still add a lesson. Nothing will be published, sent, purchased, or changed outside this workspace." Also the version-conflict guard at :210.

The sign-out dialog (app-shell.tsx:421-427) is exemplary: it names the risk, labels the destructive button honestly ("Sign out and discard drafts") rather than "OK", gives "Keep working" first, and moves focus to the safe option.

Ask Raven's cost and model disclosure at studio-page.tsx:203 ("Saved privately · {model} · Estimated model cost $…") and the per-day limit at :188 are the kind of honesty most AI products avoid. Likewise plans-page.tsx:92 "Uses AI credits. Up to 20 generations per workspace per day. No automatic approval."

The access page refuses to imply capabilities it lacks: access-page.tsx:84 "Access saved. No invitation or email was sent", :86 "Workspace access removed. Their saved work is retained", and the removal dialog at :155 says explicitly "This does not delete their account."

one-time-sign-in.tsx is careful, unpanicked and accurate in every failure branch, including the hard case at :73 where the link was consumed but authorization could not be confirmed. The closing line at :120 — "Sign-in starts only when you choose Enter my workspace" — is exactly the right consent framing.

The daily-quote figure (daily-quote.tsx) with its real Project Gutenberg citation, location and context, and the Jane Eyre line on the connected home, is the one piece of warmth in the product that is entirely earned — public-domain, attributed, verifiable, and chosen with taste.

The provenance system works: DemoBadge, "MANUAL SNAPSHOT", "NEEDS VERIFICATION", "Snapshot date unknown · Not live" (mission-control.tsx:158), the catalog footnote disclaiming a shared fictional universe (universe-catalog.tsx:127-129), and the evidence drawer's "Confidence is a review aid, not a prediction of revenue or sales." The vocabulary is consistent across every surface.

The viewer-role messaging is respectful rather than scolding, and always says what she can still do: manual-review-form.tsx:130, approval-card.tsx:143, learn-page.tsx:188 ("With viewer access, you can build, copy, and download your blueprint"). Keep that shape when rewriting the owner-gate lines.
